intro: The ReSPCT guidelines consist of 30 items divided into four sections. Each item should be reported in the main text or supplement of psychedelic clinical trial publications. A printable checklist and complementary explanatory document are also provided.

items.name: Location
items.details: Location of the trial, and whether indoors/outdoors and urban/rural/suburban.

items.name: Ambiance
items.details: Room ambiance curated by the study team.

items.name: Access to nature
items.details: Sources of nature or natural elements accessible to participants.

items.name: Objects and decorations
items.details: Objects and decorations in the room.

items.name: Lighting
items.details: Room lighting and adjustability.

items.name: Sensory reduction
items.details: Sensory reduction used, such as headphones and eyeshades.

items.name: Bathroom facilities
items.details: Level of bathroom accessibility, privacy, and safety.

items.name: Number and roles of people present
items.details: Number and roles of people present, including participants, study staff, and informal support.

items.name: Positioning
items.details: Relative position of people in the room, and what participants were positioned on.

items.name: Focus and main activities
items.details: Focus (internal or external) and main activities of the dosing session.

items.name: Music or soundscapes
items.details: Music or soundscapes that accompanied the dosing experience.

items.name: Interpersonal interventions
items.details: Verbal or physical interpersonal interventions used throughout the session.

items.name: Participant autonomy, control, and agency
items.details: Level of participant control and agency over activities and environment of the dosing session.

items.name: Dosing regimen
items.details: Dosing regimen, including drug dose(s), frequency, and length of the session.

items.name: Medical and experimental procedures or assessments
items.details: Medical and experimental procedures performed during the session.

items.name: Pre- and post-dosing protocol
items.details: Activities before and after dosing, including participant arrival and release conditions.

items.name: Potential disturbances or interruptions
items.details: Disturbances that may have impacted the dosing session.

items.name: Therapeutic or guiding approach
items.details: Therapeutic or guiding approach used throughout the study, if any, with the accompanying manual or protocol.

items.name: Narrative framing
items.details: Framing of the trial intervention by the study team, including the short- and long-term drug effects.

items.name: Number of sessions
items.details: Number and length of preparation, dosing, and integration sessions.

items.name: Preparation protocol
items.details: Activities performed during the preparation sessions.

items.name: Integration protocol
items.details: Activities performed during the integration sessions.

items.name: Additional support or follow-up
items.details: Formal or informal support or follow-up offered to participants after the end of the trial, including in the case of adverse events.

items.name: Study personnel qualifications
items.details: The credentials, training, and expertise of personnel providing the study intervention or care.

items.name: Cultural competence and safety
items.details: Study team's level of cultural competence and efforts towards cultural safety.

items.name: Therapeutic alliance
items.details: Therapeutic alliance between participants and facilitators throughout the intervention.

items.name: Trust
items.details: Participant's level of trust throughout the intervention.

items.name: Physical comfort
items.details: Participant's level of physical comfort during the dosing session.

items.name: Physical safety
items.details: Participant's sense of physical safety during the dosing session.

items.name: Psychological and cultural safety
items.details: Participant's sense of psychological and cultural safety with the people present during the dosing session.
